# Sample and Asset Inventory

Roadmap MP.1 (Appendix A3 and B6). Milestone report: [mp-1-sample-inventory.md](mp-1-sample-inventory.md).

**Date:** 2026-11-18. The two tables are generated by `SampleInventory` and kept current by `SampleInventoryTest`. The test fails when a table is stale; refresh them with `GDXUNITY_UPDATE_AUDIT=1 ./gradlew :editor-desktop:test --tests "*SampleInventoryTest"`. The text around the tables is written by hand.

This is the inventory Appendix A3 and B6 ask for before anything is downloaded or migrated: what each sample is today. **No sample is presumed broken.** Every one was loaded by the editor's own serializer, and every gallery template is opened, played and exported by the tests (section 3). Nothing was downloaded and nothing was changed.

## What it says, in short

*The counts in this section are from MP.1 (43 scenes, 149 files). MP.3 then added two opt-in migrated copies beside their originals, `platformer-tiles-2d` and `platformer-profile-terrain-25d`, and the terrain `terrains/Platformer Ground.terrain`. The tables include them (45 scenes: 8 in 2D, 8 in 2.5D, 29 in 3D); see [mp-3-conservative-migration.md](mp-3-conservative-migration.md).*

- **43 sample scenes:** 7 in 2D, 7 in 2.5D and 29 in 3D. Every one declares its dimension (`gameMode`), and every one is offered in the New Game gallery. Only three declare a genre for the Play profiles (two Action RPG, one Platformer).
- **Every scene loads**, and no scene names a file that does not exist.
- **Behaviour:**
  - 19 scenes keep their game logic in Java source, which the editor cannot show as a graph (the M1.1 "Logic FAIL"): 4 in 2D, 5 in 2.5D and 10 in 3D.
  - 2 run on graphs only: `terrain-3d` and `visual-scripting-3d`.
  - 22 have no scripts or graphs: showcases, physics demos, profile samples and landscapes.
- **Editable parts that fail** (from the M1.1 matrix):
  - Logic, and Gameplay with it, in the 19 Java scenes;
  - the baked glTF ground (Terrain) in the five landscapes and `physics-mesh-3d`;
  - glTF models with no mesh editor in 7 scenes;
  - a clip baked into a glTF in `character-creator-3d`.
- **Web player:**
  - 9 scenes are marked as playing on the web (every script ported).
  - 4 use components the web player does not have: `PlayerComponent` and `SpawnPointComponent` (the profile samples) and `EngineSound` (racing).
  - 9 scenes still need their Java scripts ported.
  - 21 use only supported components but are not marked web in the gallery. The gallery's web flag is meant for scenes whose scripts have a web port that the web tests check, so these have not been checked on the web.
- **Tests:**
  - Five scenes are named by no test of their own: `animation-samples-3d`, `depth-compositing-3d` and the three `skeleton-*` scenes. They are still covered by the tests that go through every sample (section 3).
  - 10 scenes are in the M9.5 performance baseline.
- **149 content files.** The MakeHuman data counts as one row.
  - **Formats:**

    | Format | Files | Format | Files |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | glTF | 35 | material | 9 |
    | Java | 32 | prefab | 7 |
    | anim | 20 | song | 7 |
    | graph | 20 | saved character | 4 |
    | png | 4 | sprite | 3 |
    | terrain | 3 | sculpt | 3 |
    | glb | 1 | | |

  - **Not named by any sample:**
    - 12 graphs, mostly graph versions of Java behaviour (`ArenaPlayer`, `HopperPlayer`, `RaceCar`, ...) that no scene uses yet: the M1.2 port;
    - 10 Java helper classes that other scripts call (`CarEngine`, `RaceTrack`, ...);
    - the 7 prefabs, which the level palette places;
    - 6 clips, 4 saved characters, 3 sculpts, 2 terrains, 2 songs and 2 models.

## Licences: what the repository records

| Basis | What |
|---|---|
| CC0 1.0, with a licence file | `characters/makehuman/*`: the body data the Character Creator reads ([`LICENSE-ASSETS.txt`](../../assets/characters/makehuman/LICENSE-ASSETS.txt), [`CREDITS.md`](../../assets/characters/makehuman/CREDITS.md)) |
| CC0 base data, the baked file project-made | `characters/*.gltf`: baked by the Character Creator from that data (their glTF `generator` says so) |
| Project-made, **no licence record** | Everything else: 47 files a generator in `tools/` writes or names, and 97 with no record of how they were made (made in the editor or by hand). The repository's `LICENSE` is Apache 2.0, written for the code. Whether it also covers these assets is **the owner's decision**, and no file says so |

No third-party asset was found:
- every `.gltf` names a ForgeRoom generator (one by the project's earlier name, GdxUnity) or the Character Creator;
- the one `.glb`, `models/SculptedRock.glb`, is the export of `sculpts/SculptedRock.sculpt` ([`samples/README.md`](../../assets/samples/README.md)).

That is the extent of the check. The PNG textures, songs, sprites and clips carry no provenance field, so "project-made" for them rests on the repository's history, not on a record.

**Found:** `models/BendingStrip.gltf` says it was made by `make_sample.py`, which is not in `tools/`, so it cannot be regenerated. No sample uses it.

## Migration columns (Appendix A3)

**Filled in by M2b.6** ([report](m2b-6-first-sample-refresh.md)). A3 asks for one row per scene with:
- what it uses now;
- the proposed replacement, with its source URL and licence;
- the conversion and its dependencies;
- the expected visual result, the editability level, collision and the rollback path.

The table below is generated by `SampleInventory.replacements` and kept current by `SampleInventoryTest`, like the other two tables:
- **"Shows now" and "Editability now"** are read from each scene and the M1.1 matrix.
- **The other columns** are its group's plan in the migration ledger, [`docs/migration/sample-migrations.json`](../migration/sample-migrations.json) (MC.7).
- **The last column** says, for a migrated copy, what it was made from, and for an original, its copies.

The rules that follow from this inventory for MP.3, M2b.6 and MC.7:
- The rollback path is the file itself. The shipped samples are read-only originals (roadmap R1, `SceneFileController.setReadOnlyFolder`), and a migration writes a new file beside the original.
- The scenes that are already fully data-driven are the safest first migrations: no Java logic, and every part PASS in the matrix. For example `tilemap-platformer-2d` (2D) and `platformer-profile-25d` (2.5D).

## 2. Content files

Every file in the content folders (`models`, `characters`, `sprites`, `textures`, `materials`, `terrains`, `sculpts`, `prefabs`, `animations`, `graphs`, `music`, `scripts`). "Opens in" follows `AssetOpening`. "Made by" is a glTF's own `generator` field, else a script in `tools/` whose source contains the file name ("named in": it may write or only read the file), else no record. "Named by samples" counts only what a scene names, directly or through a material, prefab or character: a Java helper class that another script calls shows none.

## 3. Tests that cover every sample

Beside the per-sample column above, these go through every scene in `assets/samples` (all passed on 2026-11-18):

| Test | What it checks for every sample |
|---|---|
| `TemplateGalleryProjectsTest` | A project made from each gallery template (all 43 samples are in the gallery) opens, compiles its scripts, plays for two seconds in the game runtime's session with no errors, and exports |
| `SampleGamesTest` | Each sample game is loaded and played headless with simulated keys (42 tests) |
| `DuplicateSampleEntitiesTest` | Every entity duplicates with all its components, and every scene saves and reopens unchanged |
| `CustomizeGatewaySamplesTest` | Every graph and clip offers its workspace, and every file an offer opens exists |
| `SceneTextDiffTest` | Every scene saves to the same text each time, and small edits give small diffs |
| `TemplateMatrixTest`, `EditabilityAuditTest` | The M1.1 matrix and audit |
| `SampleInventoryTest` | This inventory: every scene loads, declares 2d, 2.5d or 3d, and names no missing file |

Not covered for any sample: drawing (needs a display; the M9.5 baseline and editor smoke tests cover some scenes), a person's edit in each workspace, and listening.
